problem: Duolingo wanted to move faster with AI and not wait for the technology to be perfect.
title: Duolingo announces an AI-first approach, then clarifies after backlash
context: CEO Luis von Ahn posted an all-hands email on LinkedIn about becoming AI-first.
decision_made: Gradually stop using contractors for work AI can handle, and add headcount only in limited cases.
action_taken: After internal and online pushback the CEO posted a follow-up in May saying the memo was not well done, and later said he did not give enough context.
observed_outcome: A very small number of hourly contractors doing repetitive work were phased out. The CEO said the company has never laid off full-time employees and does not plan to.
lessons: Strategy memos written for staff are read by customers too, and tone and context can overwhelm the message.
limitations: Coverage tied the backlash to a 10 percent contractor reduction in January 2024. The CEO's later statements are self-reported.

claims.claim_text: Duolingo's CEO said the company would gradually stop using contractors for work AI can handle.
In August 2025 the CEO said he had not given enough context and that Duolingo has never laid off full-time employees.
